text:
Easton Cowan has been one of the few bright notes in a dark Toronto season. At 21, the 2023 first-rounder already has nine goals and 18 points in 26 games, and his ice time has jumped to about 19 minutes a night over his last ten. The Globe and Mail framed him as part of a possible silver lining to the Leafs' season, and Hockey Patrol reports he is back in trade talk as Toronto looks for a top-four defenseman.

The chances are real, but the finishing is running ahead of them: nine goals on 5.5 expected, shooting 18% after 12% last season. The bigger minutes haven't turned into more points yet either, four in his last ten against about seven our numbers expected.

What we like: last season's tracking from Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones (only nine games) had him carrying the puck in on 58% of his entries and creating a lot off the rush. What we'd watch: whether his defensive numbers hold up in heavier minutes, the weak spot in Evolving-Hockey's read on his rookie year.
headline: Cowan's goals are ahead of his game
